title: Cumulative incidence of achilles tendon rupture and tendinopathy in male former elite athletes.
journal: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To study the cumulative incidence of Achilles tendon rupture and tendinopathy among former top-level athletes.

sections.label: PARTICIPANTS
sections.text: Male former elite athlete cohort members (n = 785; median age, 69 years when responding to the questionnaire; range, 54-97) and their matched controls (n = 416; median age, 68 years; range, 56-94).

sections.label: OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS
sections.text: Questionnaire-reported Achilles tendinopathy and tendon rupture diagnosed by physicians before the age of 45 years and within the subjects' lifetimes.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Cumulative incidence of Achilles tendinopathy before the age of 45 was high for middle and long-distance runners (adjusted odds ratio, 31.2 compared with controls; P < 0.001), and cumulative incidence of Achilles tendon rupture was high for sprinters (odds ratio, 14.9; P < 0.001).

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Achilles tendon problems seem to constitute clinically significant and common problems in specific sports.
